claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in an as-cast, high-temperature BCC state.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is controlled by a kinetic nucleation barrier arising from short-range compositional inhomogeneities.
Local Al enrichment is the particularly important compositional inhomogeneity producing the proposed nucleation barrier.
The BCC-to-secondary-phase transformation is delayed until nanoscale ordered clusters reach a critical size.
Isothermal annealing at 800, 850, and 900 °C for durations ranging from minutes to hours, followed by rapid quenching, is the proposed intervention.
APT, TEM, and in situ high-temperature XRD can be used together to quantify clustering and phase evolution during the proposed comparison.
Annealing causes local compositional fluctuations to evolve into ordered B2 or FCC precursors that subsequently nucleate and grow.
The BCC phase is thermodynamically metastable at lower temperatures.
Al-enriched local inhomogeneities inhibit nucleation of the thermodynamically more stable phase.
Once compositional fluctuations attain a critical cluster size, transformation begins rapidly.
Thermodynamic instability and kinetic constraints associated with sluggish atomic mobility jointly determine phase stability.
An incubation period with no detectable new phase will precede transformation.
After a critical annealing time or at greater undercooling, FCC or B2 phases will appear rapidly and coincide with a threshold cluster size and concentration measured by APT.
The critical transformation time will decrease continuously as undercooling increases relative to the equilibrium transition temperature.
The as-cast baseline lacks significant compositional clustering.
The proposed mechanism applies in the 800–900 °C range, where diffusion is slow enough to permit accumulation of nanoscale inhomogeneities but fast enough to permit transformation.
At extreme thermal conditions, rapid diffusion may homogenize the composition and make the proposed mechanism inapplicable.
Extended homogenization provides a control expected to minimize compositional inhomogeneities and alter transformation kinetics if the mechanism is valid.
Transformation without increasing nanoscale clustering, or transformation onset that does not correlate with cluster size and density, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
